arXiv:2108.01108v1 [math.CO] 02 Aug 2021

A note on extremal intersecting linear Ryser systems

Adrián Vázquez-Ávila ††thanks: adrian.vazquez@unaq.mx Affiliation: Subdirección de Ingeniería y Posgrado Affiliation: Universidad Aeronáutica en Querétaro
Abstract

A famous conjecture of Ryser states that any rr-partite set system has transversal number at most r−1r-1 times their matching number. This conjecture is only known to be true for r≤3r\leq 3 in general, for r≤5r\leq 5 if the set system is intersecting, and for r≤9r\leq 9 if the intersecting set system is linear. In this note, we deal with Ryser’s Conjecture for intersecting rr-partite linear systems; that is, if τ\tau is the transversal number for an intersecting rr-partite linear system, then Ryser’s Conjecture states that τ≤r−1\tau\leq r-1. If this conjecture is true, this is known to be sharp for rr for which there exists a projective plane of order r−1r-1. There has also been considerable effort to find intersecting rr-partite set systems whose transversal number is r−1r-1.

In this note, the following is proved: if r≥4r\geq 4 is an even integer, then fl​(r)≥3​(r−2)+1f_{l}(r)\geq 3(r-2)+1, where fl​(r)f_{l}(r) is the minimum number of lines of an intersecting rr-partite linear system whose transversal number is r−1r-1. This lower bound gives an exact value for fl​(r)f_{l}(r), for some small values of rr. Also, we prove that any rr-partite linear system satisfies τ≤r−1\tau\leq r-1 if ν2≤r\nu_{2}\leq r for all r≥3r\geq 3 odd integer and ν2≤r−1\nu_{2}\leq r-1 for all r≥4r\geq 4 even integer, where ν2\nu_{2} is the maximum cardinality of a subset of lines R⊆ℒR\subseteq\mathcal{L} such that every triplet of different elements of RR does not have a common point.

Keywords. Ryser’s Conjecture, linear systems, transversal number, 2-packing number, projective planes

1 Introduction

A set system is a pair (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) where ℱ\mathcal{F} is a finite family of subsets on a ground set XX. A set system can be also thought of as a hypergraph, where the elements of XX and ℱ\mathcal{F} are called vertices and hyperedges respectively. The set system (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) is called rr-uniform, when all subsets of ℱ\mathcal{F} has size rr. The set system (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) is rr-partite if the elements of XX can be partitioned into rr sets X1,…,XrX_{1},\ldots,X_{r}, called the sides, such that each element of ℱ\mathcal{F} contain exactly one element of XiX_{i}, for all i=1,…,ri=1,\ldots,r, that is |F∩Xi|=1|F\cap X_{i}|=1, where F∈ℱF\in\mathcal{F}. Thus, an rr-partite set system is an rr-uniform set system.

Let (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) be a set system. A subset T⊆XT\subseteq X is a transversal of (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) if for any element F∈ℱF\in\mathcal{F} contain at least an element of TT, that is, T∩F≠∅T\cap F\neq\emptyset, for every F∈ℱF\in\mathcal{F}. The transversal number of (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}), τ=τ⁡(X,ℱ)\tau=\tau(X,\mathcal{F}), is the smallest possible cardinality of a transversal of (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}). The transversal number has been studied in the literature in many different contexts and names. For example, with the name of piercing number and covering number, see for instance [8, 9, 7, 11, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19].

Let (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) be a set system. A subset ℰ⊆ℱ\mathcal{E}\subseteq\mathcal{F} of a set system (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) is called a matching if F∩F^=∅F\cap\hat{F}=\emptyset for every F,F^∈ℰF,\hat{F}\in\mathcal{E}. The matching number of (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}), ν=ν⁡(X,ℱ)\nu=\nu(X,\mathcal{F}), is the cardinality of the largest matching of (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}). A set system is called intersecting if ν=1\nu=1; that is, F∩F^≠∅F\cap\hat{F}\neq\emptyset, for every F,F^∈ℱF,\hat{F}\in\mathcal{F}.

It is not hard to see that any rr-uniform set system (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) satisfies the inequality τ≤r​ν\tau\leq r\nu. It is well-known this bound is sharp, as shown by the family of all subsets of size rr in a ground set of size k​r−1kr-1, which has ν=k−1\nu=k-1 and τ=(k−1)​r\tau=(k-1)r. On the other hand, if ν=1\nu=1, any projective plane of order r−1r-1 (denoted by Πr−1\Pi_{r-1} in this paper), where r−1r-1 is a prime power, satisfies τ=r\tau=r. However, for rr-partite set systems, Ryser conjectured in the 1960’s that the upper bound could be improved.

Ryser’s Conjecture: Any rr-partite set system satisfies τ≤(r−1)​ν.\tau\leq(r-1)\nu.

For the special case r=2r=2, Ryser’s Conjecture is equivalent to Kőnig’s Theorem. The only other known general case of the conjecture is when r=3r=3, see [2]. However, Ryser’s conjecture is also known to be true in some special cases. Tuza verified [21] Ryser’s Conjecture for r≤5r\leq 5 if the set system is assumed intersecting. Furthermore, Francetić et al. [13] verified Ryser’s Conjecture for r≤9r\leq 9 if the set system is a linear system, that is, a set system (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) is linear if it satisfies |E∩F|≤1|E\cap F|\leq 1, for every pair of distinct subsets E,F∈ℱE,F\in\mathcal{F}. In this note every linear system is denoted by (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}), where the elements of PP and ℒ\mathcal{L} are called points and lines, respectively. In the rest of this paper, only linear systems are considered. Most of the definitions can be generalized for set systems. Thus, we deal with Ryser’s Conjecture for intersecting rr-partite linear systems.

Intersecting linear Ryser’s Conjecture: Every intersecting rr-partite linear system satisfies τ≤r−1\tau\leq r-1.

In case the conjecture would be true, it is tight in the sense that for infinitely many rr’s there are constructions of intersecting rr-partite linear systems with τ=r−1\tau=r-1. For example, if r−1r-1 is a prime power, consider the finite projective plane of order r−1r-1 as a linear system, Πr−1\Pi_{r-1}. This linear system is rr-uniform and intersecting. To make it rr-partite, one just needs to delete one point from the projective plane. This truncated projective plane gives an intersecting rr-partite linear system with τ≥r−1\tau\geq r-1, and r⁡(r−1)r(r-1) points and (r−1)2(r-1)^{2} lines, and it will be denoted by Πr−1′\Pi^{\prime}_{r-1}. However, the construction obtained from the projective plane is not the “optimal” extremal. Although the projective plane construction only contains r⁡(r−1)r(r-1) points (which is an optimal number of points), it has a lot of lines. Let f⁡(r)f(r) be the minimum integer so that there exists an intersecting rr-partite set system (X,ℱ)(X,\mathcal{F}) with τ=r−1\tau=r-1 and |ℱ|=f⁡(r)|\mathcal{F}|=f(r) lines. Analogously, let fl​(r)f_{l}(r) be the minimum integer so that there exists an intersecting rr-partite linear system (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) with τ=r−1\tau=r-1 and |ℒ|=fl​(r)|\mathcal{L}|=f_{l}(r) lines. It is probably that fl​(r)f_{l}(r) does not exist for some values of rr (if r−1r-1 is a prime power, then Πr−1′\Pi^{\prime}_{r-1} is known to exist, providing proof that fl​(r)f_{l}(r) is well-defined). Hence, if fl​(r)f_{l}(r) does exist, for some rr, then f​(r)≤fl​(r)f(r)\leq f_{l}(r). It is not difficult to prove that fl​(2)=1f_{l}(2)=1 and fl​(3)=3f_{l}(3)=3, see [15]. Furthermore, Mansour et al. [15] proved that fl​(4)=6f_{l}(4)=6 and fl​(5)=9f_{l}(5)=9. On the other hand, Aharoni et al. [3] proved that fl​(6)=13f_{l}(6)=13 and f⁡(7)=17f(7)=17 (even when the truncated projective plane does not exist, since it has been proved that finite projective planes of order six do not exist, see [20]); however Francetić proved [13] that fl​(7)f_{l}(7) does not exist, that is, there is no intersecting 77-partite linear system such that τ=6\tau=6. Abu-Khazneha et al. [1] constructed new infinite family of intersecting rr-partite set systems extremal to Ryser’s Conjecture, which exist whenever a projective plane of order r−2r-2 exists. That construction produces a large number of non-isomorphic extremal set systems. Finally, Aharoni et al. [3] gave a lower bound on f⁡(r)f(r) when r→∞r\to\infty, showing that f⁡(r)≥f(r)\geq3.052r+O⁡(1)r+O(1), this lower bound is an improvement since Mansour proved [15] that f⁡(r)≥(3−118)​r​(1−o⁡(1))≈f(r)\geq(3-\frac{1}{\sqrt{18}})r(1-o(1))\approx2.764(1−o⁡(1))(1-o(1)), when r→∞r\to\infty. In this paper, a lower bound for fl​(r)f_{l}(r) is given for r≥4r\geq 4 an even integer.

Theorem 1.1.

If r≥4r\geq 4 is an even integer, then 3​(r−2)+1≤fl​(r)3(r-2)+1\leq f_{l}(r).

Notice that, if r∈{2,4,6}r\in\{2,4,6\}, then fl​(r)=3​(r−2)+1f_{l}(r)=3(r-2)+1. Aharoni et al. [3] proved 18≤f⁡(8)18\leq f(8) and 24≤f⁡(10)24\leq f(10). Hence, by Theorem 1.1 we have: 19≤fl​(8)19\leq f_{l}(8) and 25≤fl​(10)25\leq f_{l}(10).

2 Main Results

Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be a linear system and p∈Pp\in P be a point. It is denoted by ℒp\mathcal{L}_{p} to be the set of lines incident to pp. The degree of pp is defined as d​e​g​(p)=|ℒp|deg(p)=|\mathcal{L}_{p}| and the maximum degree over all points of the linear system is denoted by Δ=Δ⁡(P,ℒ)\Delta=\Delta(P,\mathcal{L}).

A subset RR of lines of a linear system (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) is a 22-packing of (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) if the elements of RR are triplewise disjoint, that is, if any three elements are chosen in RR, then they have not a common point. The 2-packing number of (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}), ν=ν2​(P,ℒ)\nu=\nu_{2}(P,\mathcal{L}), is the maximum cardinality of a 2-packing of (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}). There are some works that study this new parameter, see [4, 5, 10, 6, 22, 24, 23, 25, 26].

Theorem 2.1.

[5] Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be a linear system with p,q∈Pp,q\in P be two points such that Δ=d​e​g​(p)\Delta=deg(p) and Δ′=max⁡{d​e​g​(x):x∈P∖{p}}\Delta^{\prime}=\max\{deg(x):x\in P\setminus\{p\}\}. If |ℒ|≤Δ+Δ′+ν2−3|\mathcal{L}|\leq\Delta+\Delta^{\prime}+\nu_{2}-3, then τ≤ν2−1\tau\leq\nu_{2}-1.

Lemma 2.2.

[22] Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be an intersecting rr-uniform linear system, with r≥3r\geq 3 be an odd integer. If τ=r\tau=r, then ν2=r+1\nu_{2}=r+1.

Corollary 2.3.

Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be an intersecting rr-partite linear system, with r≥3r\geq 3 be an odd integer. If ν2≤r\nu_{2}\leq r then τ≤r−1\tau\leq r-1.

Now, let deal with the case when rr is an even integer.

Lemma 2.4.

[24] Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be an rr-uniform intersecting linear system with r≥2r\geq 2 be an even integer. If ν2=r+1\nu_{2}=r+1 then τ=r+22\tau=\frac{r+2}{2}.

Hence, if τ>r+22\tau>\frac{r+2}{2} then ν2≤r\nu_{2}\leq r and r≥4r\geq 4.

Lemma 2.5.

[24] Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be an intersecting rr-uniform linear system, with r≥4r\geq 4 be an even integer. If τ=r\tau=r, then ν2=r\nu_{2}=r.

Lemma 2.6.

Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be an intersecting rr-uniform linear system with r≥4r\geq 4 be an even integer. If τ=r−1\tau=r-1, then ν2=r\nu_{2}=r.

Proof. Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be an intersecting rr-partite linear system. Let p,q∈Pp,q\in P be two points such that Δ=d​e​g​(p)\Delta=deg(p) and Δ′=max⁡{d​e​g​(x):x∈P∖{p}}\Delta^{\prime}=\max\{deg(x):x\in P\setminus\{p\}\}. By Theorem 2.1 if |ℒ|≤Δ+Δ′+ν2−3≤3​(r−2)+1|\mathcal{L}|\leq\Delta+\Delta^{\prime}+\nu_{2}-3\leq 3(r-2)+1, then τ≤ν2−1\tau\leq\nu_{2}-1, which implies that ν2=r\nu_{2}=r.      

Corollary 2.7.

Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be an intersecting rr-partite linear system with r≥4r\geq 4 be an even integer. If ν2≤r−1\nu_{2}\leq r-1 then τ≤r−2\tau\leq r-2.

By Lemmas 2.5 and 2.6, we have:

Corollary 2.8.

Let (P,ℒ)(P,\mathcal{L}) be an intersecting rr-uniform linear system with r≥4r\geq 4 be an even number. If τ∈{r−1,r}\tau\in\{r-1,r\}, then ν2=r\nu_{2}=r.

By Corollaries 2.3 and 2.7, and Lemma 2.5, we have:

Theorem 2.9.

Let r≥3r\geq 3 be an integer. Then every intersecting rr-partite linear system satisfies

  1. 1.

    τ≤r−1\tau\leq r-1 If ν2≤r\nu_{2}\leq r and r≥3r\geq 3 be an odd integer; and

  2. 2.

    τ≤r−2\tau\leq r-2 if ν2≤r−1\nu_{2}\leq r-1 and r≥4r\geq 4 be an even integer.

The intersecting linear Ryser’s Conjecture is almost proved; it only remains to analyzes two cases concerning the 2-packing number:

Conjecture 2.10.

Let r≥3r\geq 3 be an integer. Then every intersecting rr-partite linear system satisfies:

  1. 1.

    τ≤r−1\tau\leq r-1 if ν2=r+1\nu_{2}=r+1, with r≥3r\geq 3 an odd number.

  2. 2.

    τ≤r−1\tau\leq r-1 if ν2=r\nu_{2}=r, with r≥4r\geq 4 an even number.

Theorem 2.11.

Let r≥4r\geq 4 be an even integer, then 3​(r−2)+1≤fl​(r)3(r-2)+1\leq f_{l}(r).

Proof. Suppose that ν2≤r−1\nu_{2}\leq r-1 (by Corollary 2.8). Let p,q∈Pp,q\in P be two points such that d​e​g​(p)=Δdeg(p)=\Delta and Δ′=deg⁡(q)=max⁡{d​e​g​(x):x∈P∖{p}}\Delta^{\prime}=\deg(q)=\max\{deg(x):x\in P\setminus\{p\}\}. By Theorem 2.1 if |ℒ|≤Δ+Δ′+ν2−3≤3​(r−2)|\mathcal{L}|\leq\Delta+\Delta^{\prime}+\nu_{2}-3\leq 3(r-2), then τ≤ν2−1≤r−2\tau\leq\nu_{2}-1\leq r-2. Therefore, 3​(r−2)+1≤fl​(r)3(r-2)+1\leq f_{l}(r).
